Hello,

could you record REF_f10a9088 as the appraisal decision ID for the research notebooks we reviewed on Tuesday?

The notebooks span the early furnace trials and include drawings that were never transferred into the final engineering reports. We agreed to retain the original bound volumes because the margins show how the measurements were interpreted at the time. The loose photocopies made later for a conference display can be removed after the archive confirms that every annotated page appears in the bound set. I spoke with the retired engineer who donated them, and she clarified that the blue cover marks a different trial series, not a second copy of the red volume. Please keep that distinction in the description. The appraisal ID should connect the decision to the accession record and the donor's note. It does not authorize a general cleanup of the research shelves.

If the archive finds an unlisted loose page, hold it for another look before any copy is removed. I will help compare handwriting if the page has no date.

Hello All!

Just wanted to give you guys an update.  The weather looks good for the
garage sale this weekend.  So that is a good thing.

If you want to bring your stuff by Friday evening, that might be a good plan
for us all to get things set up.  That way all we have to do saturday
morning is drag the tables out of the garage.  Also, I do not have a rack
for hanging clothes, so they will have to be folded or hung on the fence.

How about coming over friday evening around 630-7pm.  Also, if you have any
card tables, please bring them.  I have one and am borrowing two from my
parents.  But I am sure we may need a couple of more.

I bought a couple of garage sale signs on Monday and plan to put them out on
the main street, South Braeswood.  Another idea would be for us to take out
an ad in the greensheet.  Someone told me they cost around $15.  I am in the
process of getting some info as to the exact cost and will let you know when
i get the info confirmed. I am leaving that up to the majority vote as to
whether we all chip in for the add or not.  I think it may be worth it, some
people look for those adds and spend all day saturday doing garage sales.
But whatever you guys think

The hours of the Sale will be from 7am-1230ish.  I think by then whatever
doesn't sale either goes home or to goodwill.  I know some of you cant be
there all day or right at 7am, but I will need some help so let me know what
time you plan on coming over that morning.

Ok, so to summarize all my chatter, 3 questions, 1:  do we take out an ad in
the greensheet?   2: are you coming over friday to set up? and 3:  what time
will you be there on sat?

See ya

Jennifer

Weather forecasts would indicate low demand conditions through the
Thanksgiving Holiday's.  TEXAS EASTERN TRANSMISSION (TE) is facing high
line pack levels and full storage.  Thus the pipe has severely
restricted ability to absorb due-shipper gas.  Effective immediately,
and continuing through the end of the month, TE is requiring that:
     -    All shippers ensure their physical receipts do not exceed  physical
       deliveries.
     -    Receipt operators are expected to not flow above scheduled volumes.
     -    Delivery meters are expected to take all gas scheduled.
     -    Any customer who is long should take immediate action to resolve
       due-shipper positions.

No due-pipeline makeup gas may be scheduled. OBA parties should ensure
that physical takes match scheduled nominations. Due-shipper makeup gas
may be scheduled through your Operations Account Manager.  These
restrictions are expected to be in effect until further notice.

Please contact your Operations Account Manager if you have any
questions.

Reminder to file under long-term notes: Hello, could you forward the approved errata for the turbine control software manual to c_41429ae8@relay.example.net?

The engineering archive is preparing a historical edition for the maintenance teams, and several page corrections arrived after the last printed binder was issued. The errata identify a mislabeled terminal diagram and a table whose units were printed in the wrong column. Those changes matter when someone compares an old maintenance entry with the current digital manual. Please send the editor's signed errata sheet and the page references together. A message saying only that the manual was updated will not let the archivist annotate the historical binder. We keep older editions because field logs cite their page numbers; removing them would make those logs harder to interpret. The current operating procedure remains in the controlled document system and is the version technicians use for live work. I spoke with the documentation lead about the diagram. She confirmed that the wire colors in the drawing are correct, but the terminal labels were transposed. That precise distinction should appear in the archive note. One of the old binders also contains a handwritten margin correction from a technician. Please leave that handwriting visible when the archive makes its scan, even if the approved errata express the correction more clearly. It shows what staff understood before the formal update. If the editor sends a revised errata sheet tomorrow, forward the revised signed copy as a separate message with its approval date. The archivist can then preserve the sequence and mark which sheet applies to each edition. After the transfer, I will review the archive description against the current document index. We want a reader to find the right historical page while still seeing the correction that followed it.

Thanks, S. Mbaye

On Thu, 7 Feb 2002, Robert Lundqvist wrote:

I have tried to find a neat way to include graphs from R in LaTeX documents,
but have not succeeded (I work with a WinEdt/MikTeX combination). The two
roads I have stumbled along so far are the following:
>
*Generate postscript files and convert them into EPS files by means of
GhostScript or other not so straightforward tools.

Generate .eps directly by using dev.copy2eps or from the menu on the
graphics window or by following the instructions in ?postscript.
No conversion should be needed.

*Generate pictex files and include these.

That driver does work but is minimally-featured.  Not recommended.

None of these solutions have worked so far. I haven't spent so much time
trying to find out what goes wrong, but since there might both LaTeX gurus
and R wizards among you, I simply thought it would be better to lean on that
expertize first. Any suggestions about how to achieve what really should be
a simple task?

It really is a simple task.  Use dev.copy2eps and then the graphicx
package in latex.  You give us no clue as to your problems, so it is
difficult to give any advice.

Please change the destination for field turbine maintenance permit updates to c_8ce74fa8@relay.example.net. The scheduler is coordinating two crews at the hilltop site, where access depends on a narrow weather window.

The electrical isolation permit is expected to be approved first; the lifting permit may follow only after the wind forecast is reviewed. Each approval must reach the scheduler with its own permit number and valid hours. A combined summary would make it too easy to overlook a shorter lifting window. The crane company has reserved Tuesday morning, but the crew will not travel until both permits and the site access notice are current. The spare gearbox seal is already on site and has been checked against the work order. If weather shifts, the operations supervisor will issue a new schedule, while the permit office will amend the valid hours. Please route those amended permit messages as well. Keep completed inspection forms in the maintenance system, where the asset engineer can review them after the work. I will compare permit times with crew availability at the afternoon planning call. If a permit is delayed beyond Tuesday, the scheduler needs the original decision and the revised expected time so the crane reservation can be changed.

Thank you, C. Duarte

Hi,

please put REF_aeb735da in the decision ID field for network interconnection capacity studies that move from the preliminary queue into detailed review. The west feeder has attracted several solar projects, but the preliminary estimates assume a transformer upgrade that has not been approved. I want each applicant's study record to show whether it is awaiting a detailed engineering decision or merely an initial screening response. The project developer may ask why the available capacity looks different from last quarter's map. The map used older demand assumptions, while the current queue includes a large industrial connection that has reserved part of the feeder. Please attach the study date and assumptions to the decision record so we can explain that difference accurately. Last week the planning engineer identified a possible alternative route through the southern substation. It might provide capacity for one smaller project, but its protection settings still need analysis. Do not describe that route as approved in applicant correspondence yet.

The ID will help us find the studies ready for technical review, not grant a connection offer. The network team will send a formal offer only after voltage, fault level, and protection checks are complete. I spoke with the customer team about the two applications due for updates in November; they would rather receive an honest status note than another provisional capacity figure. We can send that note with a target date for the next engineering review. Keep all prior study versions in the planning archive because their assumptions explain how the queue evolved. If an applicant withdraws, record the withdrawal separately and let planning recalculate available capacity at the next published update. I will review the detailed study queue with engineering on Friday.

Cheers, M. Tanaka

Delete obsolete restore rehearsal image REF_c3fcf437. The image was created during the May backup exercise and has since been replaced by a verified June restore set. Keep the June set, its checksum record, and the production backup chain. The May image contains a partial application database captured before the final configuration was applied. It was useful for rehearsing the restore sequence but cannot represent the current service. The operations log records that the May rehearsal booted successfully; that log should remain even after the image is removed. During this week's storage review, the older image appeared in the same selection menu as the verified set. That creates an avoidable chance of choosing the wrong source during a future rehearsal. Confirm the May image identifier against the rehearsal log before deletion. Do not remove any incremental backup that feeds the production chain. The storage engineer checked dependencies yesterday and found that this image is independent of the June set, but the operator performing the deletion should verify the displayed identifier once more. The June restore set was exercised with the current authentication service and the updated reporting database. Its runbook and recovery timings are in the continuity folder. Keep the incident snapshot from April as well; it has a separate retention requirement tied to the outage review. The image named here is only the obsolete rehearsal copy. After removal, record the storage volume released and the image identifier in the maintenance ticket.

The capacity report for next month can then use the revised free space figure.

If the dependency view differs from the engineer's note, pause the deletion and send me the discrepancy.

I will have storage review it before changing any backup content.
emails.subject: RE: Old restore rehearsal image

emails.body:
Rick,
How are you doing?

Where is Steve off too?  Did he even say goodbye?

I'm still perseverating over Enron.  I can't help myself.  Horrible
time to be laid off -- can't talk to be people to find work because
everyone is on vacation.

I've heard lots of rumors about severance.  Has Enron asked or is it
planning to ask the BK court for real severance for employees already
dumped or is its plan only to seek real severance for those who were
kept on after Dec 3?  I finally got my expense check deposited.  That
was welcome.  What about all our vendors? Did they get screwed too?
All - or some -- do we pay our utility bill but not our $500 bill to
the AReM lobbyist?  Do we pay Safeway for drinks for the fridge, but
not our $3000 retainer to Dan Douglass?  This all seems arbitrary,
crass and unfair.  How can Ken Lay look at himself in the mirror
every day knowing how many employees he has harmed?  I can understand
how the Company cannot control the stock market and the effects of
that implosion, but I cannot understand how can the Company can
brazenly cut so many people with only a $4500, less taxes, etc.,
check as so-called severance -- not even paying accrued vacation .  I
and many others would feel a lot better about the Company if our
rights and good will hadn't been trampled on.

I haven't been able to look for work much -- no one is around.  So, I
guess I'm spending too much time thinking about this stuff.

Here comes 2002, Thank God!

Sue Mara
164 Springdale Way
Emerald Hills, CA 94062
Cell:  (415) 902-4108
Home: (650) 369-8268
